witness_rule: A zero run closes only as the minimal fill before an object requesting alignment N: the previous canonical carve's compiled data section ends exactly at the run and equals the original on every non-relocation bit; the next object is the canonical carve starting at the run's end (same proof) whose pinned compiled .s requests N for the section's first object, equal to the section's ELF alignment, or a replayed g++ vtable starting there, for which the vtable layer's pinned cc1plus probe requests N = 8; the next start is N-aligned in VRAM and the run is shorter than N. Zero bytes, geometry or a section alignment alone never qualify. No C/C++ or owned-data credit.
assumption: Constructive minimal-fill allocation in the witnessed reconstruction, not proof of historical layout: N is the alignment the matched reconstruction's compiler requests for the next object (its source type, the compiler's own jump-table .align 3, or cc1plus's vtable .align 3); an unreferenced zero object hidden inside a run shorter than N cannot be excluded by bytes alone.
